latestAuditorResult.report:
I'm approving this. Every success criterion now has evidence, and each point from the last rejection has been dealt with.

**What I checked**
- **Separate package:** there's still no `src/ornith`, but the user did approve that. The session log has the user's answer at 13:49 on 2026-10-25: "Accept shared engine (Recommended)". `docs/work/ORNITH_VERIFICATION.md` records the decision.
- **Benchmarks:** `docs/work/ORNITH_BENCH.md` has the full table with the commands for both engines, all measured on this machine. Strata beats llama.cpp's best tuned config on every row:

  | Test | llama.cpp best tuned | Strata |
  |---|---|---|
  | pp512 | 181.5 | 213.4 / 226.6 |
  | pp2048 | 532.8 | 569.5 |
  | pp4096 | 875.6 | 985.9 |
  | tg128 | 14.45 | 15.9–19.4 |
  | 256-token chat decode | 14.1 | 18.1 (19.3 with `--mtp 1`) |

  The pp4096 number uses a non-default setting (`STRATA_Q36_CHUNK=4096`), and the doc says so.
- **Correctness against llama.cpp:**
  - The logit test (`tools/qwen35/ornith_kl.py`) gives Strata a mean KL of 0.0252. llama.cpp run with a different GPU/CPU split, as a noise floor, gives 0.0381.
  - Over the real `strata launch --family ornith` server, the chat answer, the `get_weather` tool call and the Anthropic reply match llama-server's exactly.
  - The llama.cpp side is saved in `ornith-evidence/api_llamacpp.txt`. The Strata side appears in the doc table, and the session log shows the launch actually ran and served those answers.
- **Qwen and DeepSeek paths:**
  - Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ2_XS gives the same output tokens with the main build and the branch build, in both default and `--expert-cache 4` modes (`qwen38_main_vs_branch.txt`).
  - `src/dsv41` is untouched. DeepSeek does call the CPU-pool format check, which the branch changed. That new check only rejects expert sizes the old limits already rejected, so it can't change what DeepSeek accepts.
  - DeepSeek and Qwen3.6 weren't run because neither model is on this machine. The doc notes that gap.
- **Tests:**
  - `pytest tests/terminal` has the same 28 failures on main and on the branch, with identical failure lists; the branch passes 1646.
  - The 7 new tests in `test_launch_ornith.py` pass.
  - ctest on the branch fails 3 tests, all of which also fail on main (main fails 4).
- **Branch:** the work is on `ornith-support` in 12 incremental commits, not pushed.

**Remaining gaps**
- There's no SSD tier for this model. All 48 GiB of experts fit in the 61 GB of RAM, so it isn't needed.
- The Strata half of the API comparison isn't saved as a raw file in the repo; it's only in the doc table and the session log.

<approved/>

I'm approving this. Every criterion in the objective and the verification contract checks out against the repository itself, not just the executor's claim.

- **Benchmark doc:** `docs/work/ORNITH_BENCH.md` has a "Speed round 2" section.
  - Each of the six ideas has before/after numbers, a sweep, or a reason it was skipped with numbers (KV precision, per-layer slot split, the new IQ3_S layout).
  - The final table covers everything required: pp512, pp2048, pp4096, tg128, and 256-token chat with and without `--mtp 1`, plus the commands.
  - `~/work/fullbench.sh` exists and matches the commands the doc describes.
- **Defaults:** in `src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu`, around line 4520, the four kept changes are switched on only when the model has Ornith's geometry (n_embd 3072, expert width 1024). They only fill in a value if the user hasn't set one. Those four are `STAGE_SPLIT`, `FETCH_CACHE`, `FETCH_ADAPT` (step 0.005) and `IQ_MT_MIN=1`. The changes that measured no faster need an explicit flag to turn on: `EMBD_CPU`, `PROFILE`, `PREFETCH`, `NGRAM`, `--draft-vocab` and `CHUNK=4096`.
- **Quality check:** `ornith_kl_round2.txt` shows mean KL 0.0256 against a noise floor of 0.0381 (0.67x, limit 1.5x): PASS.
- **Qwen3.8 Flash-Next:** `qwen38_main_vs_branch_round2.txt` shows identical tokens in all four runs (main and branch builds, default and low-VRAM).
- **pytest:** 29 failures on the branch against main's 28.
  - The extra one is `test_serve_kill_parent`. It passed 3 of 3 reruns on both the branch and main, so I accept the executor's call that it's a flaky timing test. That's the one judgement call I made.
- **ctest:** the branch fails the same 4 tests as main.
- **Git:** the branch is clean and up to date with `fork/ornith-support`. `git ls-remote` on the fork shows `ornith-support` at 7efcfd96, which matches HEAD. The work went in as incremental commits.

**Two limits on this audit:**
- I didn't rerun the GPU benchmarks, so the speed numbers rest on the recorded runs.
- `STAGE_SPLIT` alone was mixed: tg128 after pp2048 went from 15.8 to 15.2. It improved chat decode and is what `FETCH_CACHE` builds on, so keeping it on is reasonable.

<approved/>

recentEventsByGoal.report:
I'm not approving this yet. The benchmarks and the logit comparison look solid. But one explicit requirement wasn't met, and several others only have the executor's word behind them.

**What holds up**
- **Branch and commits:** the work is on `ornith-support`, committed in 11 small steps, with nothing pushed.
- **Benchmarks:** `docs/work/ORNITH_BENCH.md` has a full table with commands for both engines. Strata beats llama.cpp's best tuned config on every row:

  | Test | llama.cpp best tuned | Strata |
  |---|---|---|
  | pp512 | 181.5 | 213 / 227 |
  | pp2048 | 532.8 | 569.5 |
  | pp4096 | 875.6 | 985.9 |
  | tg128 | 14.45 | 15.9–19.4 |
  | 256-token chat decode | 14.1 | 18.1 |

  - pp512 was a loss (153.4) as of the t6 entry in the goal log. The later commit `c25f908f` fixed it and the doc shows the sweep.
  - The pp4096 result uses `STRATA_Q36_CHUNK=4096`, which isn't the default; the doc says so.
- **Logit correctness:** the doc records a full-vocabulary comparison against llama.cpp. Strata's mean KL is 0.024; llama.cpp against itself with a different GPU/CPU split gives 0.032. The script is `tools/qwen35/ornith_kl.py`.
- **Launch wiring:** `setup.py` handles the two-file GGUF with checksum checks, there's a catalog entry, and there are 7 tests in `tests/terminal/test_launch_ornith.py`.
- **SSD tier:** leaving it out is justified. All 48 GiB of experts fit in RAM.

**Why I'm disapproving**
1. **No separate model package.** The goal asked for one, modelled on `src/dsv41`. There's no `src/ornith`. Ornith runs through the shared Qwen engine (`src/qwen35/q36_engine.cu`, ~395 lines changed), with its defaults switched on by detecting the model's shape. That may be a reasonable engineering choice, since the architecture is the same `qwen35moe`. But it contradicts what was asked, and the executor never asked the user, as the goal's instructions said to.
2. **"Qwen/DeepSeek unchanged" is reasoned, not measured.** Code those paths also use was changed:
   - the CPU pool buffer sizes (`pool.hpp`, `native_expert.hpp`);
   - the list of accepted down-projection formats in `iq_kernels.cu`;
   - load-time re-encoding of mismatched gate/up types in `q36_engine.cu`;
   - the download/size helpers in `setup.py`.

   The goal required proof from existing tests or benchmarks. No Qwen or DeepSeek benchmark or before/after comparison is recorded anywhere. The executor only argues that the changes "only enlarge buffers or accept types refused before".
3. **API check through `strata launch` isn't recorded.** The chat, tool-call and Anthropic results checked against llama.cpp appear only in the executor's claim and the goal log ("chat/tool/Anthropic OK"). There's no transcript, log or doc entry.
4. **Test results aren't recorded or reproducible here.** The verification contract asked for pytest results, but none are saved in the repo. "28 pre-existing failures on main" and "ctest failures are a subset of main's" are unsupported. I couldn't re-run anything: this environment has no `python` command and `python3` has no pytest installed.

**To approve:**
- Either add a separate Ornith package or get the user to accept reusing the Qwen engine.
- Record a Qwen (and, where possible, DeepSeek) before/after benchmark or test run showing identical behaviour.
- Save the launch-path chat, tool-call and Anthropic transcripts compared with llama.cpp.
- Record the actual pytest and ctest output for both this branch and main.

activity.objective:
=== Goal ===
Objective: Add Ornith-1.5-122B (bartowski GGUF, first target IQ3_XS) support to Strata as a separate model package (modeled on how DeepSeek/dsv41 was added in src/dsv41 + launch/TUI wiring), reusing Strata's Qwen3.8-Flash-Next optimizations (VRAM→RAM→SSD tiered expert caching, MoE kernels, prefill/spec paths, etc.), so it runs on this machine (RTX 3090 Ti 24 GB, 61 GB RAM, 16 cores, Linux) faster than llama.cpp.

Success criteria:
- `strata launch --family ornith` (model IQ3_XS) downloads/locates the GGUF, starts the server, and the OpenAI/Anthropic-compatible API returns coherent output (chat + a tool call) verified against llama.cpp reference output/logits on the same GGUF.
- Measured on this machine with the same GGUF and comparable context: Strata decode tok/s AND prefill tok/s both beat llama.cpp's best tuned config (-ngl / -ot / --n-cpu-moe, flash-attn, threads tuned). Numbers and exact commands recorded in a doc.
- New tests (tests/terminal style, plus engine correctness test) pass; existing `python -m pytest tests/terminal` has no new failures.
- Qwen/DeepSeek default paths unchanged (byte-identical behavior; verified by existing tests/bench).

Boundaries:
- In scope: research (repo + external: llama.cpp, model architecture/config), engine package for Ornith, GGUF loader/quant kernels needed for IQ3_XS, tiered caching, server integration, strata CLI launch/family wiring, tests, a doc with measurements.
- Out of scope / optional: desktop app UI, translations, other quant sizes beyond IQ3_XS (can be noted as follow-ups), pushing or opening PRs.

Constraints:
- Work on a new git branch; commit incrementally; never push or open a PR.
- No claims without measurement; report only numbers produced on this machine.
- Follow AGENTS.md/CONTRIBUTING.md style; new feature is opt-in.
- Build every backend touched where possible (CUDA here); note un-built backends.


If blocked: stop and ask the user (e.g., unknown architecture details, hardware limits making the llama.cpp-beating target infeasible — report evidence first).
